newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate soars as players head for bourse.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate soars as players head for bourse.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates retreated from an earlier increase, but still closed up 305 basis points on Thursday.
Dealers said rates soared on a liquidity squeeze exacerbated by foreign dealers switching from the money market into stocks.
"Banks with liquidity and those with paper have been at war for some days now," a fixed-income analyst said.
Dealers said several banks were short on liquidity with which to settle balances outstanding on checking accounts they hold with the central bank by the August 6 deadline.
The Mexican bolsa soared 1.88 percent to close at a record 5,067.83 points on Thursday due to foreign buying, traders said.

Banco de Mexico earlier drained 1.513 billion pesos from the market through three direct Cetes sales and three repos. Dealers said this move tightened the ongoing liquidity squeeze and added to upside pressure on rates.
Overnight rates on bank paper rose 100 basis points to close at 20.00 percent.
Liquidity of 2.564 billion pesos was scheduled to return to the system from prior central bank participation.
